title: Clopen dimension loci in proper smooth connected families
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $f:X\to S$ be proper and smooth [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and suppose its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are nonempty and connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], with dimension at most an integer $d\ge0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For $0\le i\le d$ let $S_i$ be the set of points whose geometric fibre has dimension $i$. These sets are pairwise disjoint open and closed subsets covering $S$. With their open subscheme structures [def-weil-open-immersion], the base changes $f_i:X\times_S S_i\to S_i$ [def-pc-base-change] are proper and smooth with nonempty geometrically connected fibres of pure dimension $i$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. The morphism $f_0$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 02G1, label lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free, with proper closed images of the rank loci; Tag 01TH, label lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, zero-dimensional fibre criterion. Agent-formulated consequence.

proof.text: Put $r(x)=\dim_x(X_{f(x)})$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], $r$ is locally constant. Its values are nonnegative finite integers by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension]. Thus $U_n=\{x:r(x)=n\}$ is open and closed: local constancy makes both $U_n$ and its complement unions of open neighbourhoods on which $r$ is constant. The $U_n$ are disjoint and cover $X$.

For $s\in S$, [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure] applied to $X_s$ shows that the assumed connected geometric fibre makes $X_s$ geometrically connected, hence nonempty and connected. Identify its underlying space with $f^{-1}(s)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The trace of each $U_n$ is clopen in this connected space. At any point of the nonempty fibre choose its value $n$; its trace is nonempty, so its clopen complement is empty by [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Consequently $r$ is constant with value $n$ on the whole fibre.

The restriction $U_n\to S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Its fibre at a point of $U_n$ is an open subspace of the fibre of $f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], and its dimension there is still $n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace]. Hence it is smooth of relative dimension $n$ in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], its base change to an algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$. For an $s$ whose fibre has the constant value $n$ of step 2, that base change is the whole geometric fibre: all of $X_s$ lies in $U_n$. The equivalence in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with nonempty equidimensional fibres therefore shows that both $X_s$ and its geometric fibre have pure dimension $n$, and hence dimension $n$. Thus $n\le d$ by the assumed bound, and $f(U_i)=S_i$, $f^{-1}(S_i)=U_i$.

Properness means universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $f$ is a closed map. Since $U_i$ and $X\setminus U_i$ are closed, $f(U_i)=S_i$ and $f(X\setminus U_i)$ are closed. Saturation from step 3 and the nonemptiness of every fibre give $f(X\setminus U_i)=S\setminus S_i$: a fibre meeting one of these two complementary saturated subsets lies entirely there. Thus $S_i$ is also open. Every nonempty fibre has exactly one value $i$ between $0$ and $d$, so the $S_i$ are pairwise disjoint and cover $S$.

Equip $S_i$ with its open subscheme structure. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change], $f_i$ is proper and smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], $X\times_S S_i$ is the open subscheme $f^{-1}(S_i)=U_i$ of $X$. At $s\in S_i$, [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies the structure sheaf with the restriction of that of $S$. Taking the direct limit of sections over open neighbourhoods of $s$ gives the same local ring, and taking its quotient by the maximal ideal gives the same residue field; the fibre products defining the ordinary and geometric fibres of $f_i$ are therefore those of $f$. By [def-pc-base-change] these are the same fibre products, so step 2 gives nonempty geometrically connected ordinary fibres and step 3 gives geometric fibres of pure dimension $i$. In particular the restricted family retains all the asserted fibre properties.

Properness gives finite type for $f_0$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $s\in S_0$, its ordinary fibre has dimension zero by steps 3 and 5 and is of finite type over $\kappa(s)$, using [lem-pc-proper-base-change] on $f_0$. Apply [lem-sc-dim0-finite] to the whole fibre, a closed subset of itself: it is a finite set of closed points. For each point, the complement of its singleton is a finite union of closed singletons and is closed, so the singleton is open. Every point is therefore isolated in its fibre, and the finite-type, isolated-fibre-point definition [pqf-def-quasifinite] gives that $f_0$ is quasi-finite. If $S_0$ is empty this assertion is vacuous.
